paper text.text:
Every torus embedding of $\Psi_1$ is cellular with five faces.
For some $k\in\{1,2,3\}$, put
$\{i,j\}=\{1,2,3\}\setminus\{k\}$. There are $x,y\in\{i,j\}$, possibly equal, for which the
boundary walks meet the paths $P_1,P_2,P_3$ as follows,
with the intermediate twins omitted in (i) and (ii).
\begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(\roman*)}]
\item The boundary walk of each of the two \emph{simple faces}
contains both $P_i$ and $P_j$ and meets no other path.
In each walk, these paths occur in the order
$s_iP_it_i,\,t_jP_j^{-1}s_j$.
\item The boundary walk of the \emph{repeated face} traverses
$P_k$ once in each direction and meets $P_i\cup P_j$ exactly
at $s_x$ and $t_y$. Its order is
$s_kP_kt_k,\,t_y,\,t_kP_k^{-1}s_k,\,s_x$.
We call $P_k$ the \emph{repeated path}.
\item The boundary walk of one remaining face meets the paths
exactly at $s_k$ and $s_{x'}$. The boundary walk of the other remaining face
meets them exactly at $t_k$ and $t_{y'}$, where
$\{x,x'\}=\{y,y'\}=\{i,j\}$.
\end{enumerate}
All twelve triples $(k,x,y)$ occur. Hence the path vertices
on any face boundary, or on the boundaries of all faces
incident with an internal vertex of a path, lie in some
$V(P_\ell)\cup V(P_m)$ or
$V(P_\ell)\cup\{s_m,t_n\}$ with $m,n\ne\ell$.
\end{lemma}
\begin{proof}
The graph $\Psi_1$ is connected and nonplanar, as $\Psi_1-z$ is a subdivision of
$K_{3,3}$ with parts $A_1$ and $\{p,q,r\}$, so its torus embeddings are
cellular by Youngs's theorem. Subdividing an edge does not change the faces,
so we may take each $P_i$ to be an edge. Up to automorphisms of $\Psi_1$, there are exactly two torus embeddings~\supp{R1}. The last assertion follows from
(i)--(iii), as an internal vertex of a path lies only on the faces at its
two edges.
\end{proof}

order $C$. For $B_a$ in $H_{\mathrm{rep}}$, and for $B_b$ in $H_{\mathrm{simp}}$,
the remaining graph contains the path through the four attachments
described above. Only its internal attachments can separate
the others, and its two end segments cannot alternate on
the face boundary. This gives the two four-cycles, the
path and the two triangles with a pendant edge containing
that path.

For $B_b$ in $H_{\mathrm{rep}}$, the edges $ac,bd$ remain.
No other attachment can separate either pair, and the two pairs cannot
alternate on a face boundary. This excludes the star and
leaves the two four-cycles, four paths and four triangles
with a pendant edge containing $ac,bd$. If the remaining
graph is disconnected, each component meets an attachment,
so there are exactly two components, containing $a,c$ and
$b,d$. The face containing the deleted interior is then
an annulus, giving the completion $B_b+ac+bd$.

Corollary~\ref{cor:boundary-completions} tests each reduced
disk boundary, and Lemma~\ref{lem:annulus-embedding} tests
the annulus. If the original bridge and its minor have the
same planar listed completions, we can insert the original
bridge and restore the discarded boundary parts. Thus
$H_{\mathrm{simp}}$ or $H_{\mathrm{rep}}$ remains planar with all
the other bridges present. For $B_b$, the allowed minor retains a path
from $a$ to $b$ through its connected interior to replace $P_m$.
Hence, by Lemma~\ref{dis:joint-test}, a torus embedding after
the replacement gives one of $G$. Conversely, the graph
obtained by the replacement is a minor of $G$, so it is
toroidal whenever $G$ is.
The boundary orders of $\Psi_1$ used above are recorded in~\supp{R1}.
\end{proof}

what: Every rotation system of Psi_1 with P_1, P_2, P_3 the edges s1t1, s2t2, s3t3 (subdividing an edge does not change the faces). Attachments: the path vertices s1, t1, s2, t2, s3, t3; twins omitted. Vertex names in a sequence are separated by spaces.
how to read: For each graph: 'cyclic orders' lists, for every vertex, all cyclic orders of its neighbours, each starting with its alphabetically first neighbour (the other neighbours follow in every possible order, in lexicographic order). Rotation system number i (counting from 0) takes at each vertex the cyclic order whose position is the corresponding digit of i, written in the mixed radix given by the numbers of cyclic orders in the order of 'vertices', the last vertex varying fastest (the order of Python's itertools.product). Facial walks are traced by the rule used throughout the supplement: after the dart u->v comes v->w, where w follows u in the cyclic order at v. The genus is (2 - V + E - F)/2. The attachment sequence of a facial walk lists the attachments it passes through, in walk order, one entry per passage; it is written from its lexicographically least cyclic shift, keeping the direction of the walk, and the faces of a row are sorted. Since many rotation systems give the same row, the distinct rows are listed once under 'distinct rows' and 'rows' gives, for every rotation system in order, the position of its row in that list. 'Up to cyclic shift and reversal' in the claims means the least sequence among all cyclic shifts of the sequence and of its reverse.

claims.statement: Psi_1 is nonplanar and every torus embedding has five faces (Lemma 4.2).
Up to automorphisms of Psi_1, there are exactly two torus embeddings (proof of Lemma 4.2).

Lemma 4.2: every torus rotation has, for exactly one triple (k,x,y), two simple faces with sequence s_i t_i t_j s_j, a repeated face s_k t_k t_y t_k s_k s_x, and faces s_k s_x' and t_k t_y' ({i,j} = {1,2,3} - {k}, {x,x'} = {y,y'} = {i,j}); all twelve triples occur.

Proof of Lemma 4.27: a choice with k = w gives the boundary a, c, P_x, d, b on each side of P_m, that is, the two faces at the edge s_m t_m are distinct and both have sequence s_m t_m t_x s_x up to cyclic shift and reversal (checked for every torus rotation and every m other than k).

Proof of Lemma 4.27, for B_a with attachments s_x, t_x, s_y, t_y: a choice with k = w has simple faces s_x t_x t_y s_y (the cycle C), and the choice (x,y,y) has the repeated face s_x t_x t_y t_x s_x s_y, with s_x, t_x twice and s_y, t_y once.
